text: Urban transportation is undergoing major transformations, driven in part by the emergence of new technologies—some of which are being developed in Toronto—and accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. These shifts are putting pressure on public streets to be used in new and unanticipated ways, while also presenting potential opportunities to improve the transportation system. Like the broader category of smart city technologies, many transportation innovations bring new challenges for cities in terms of safety, accessibility, cybersecurity, privacy, and decision-making. The City of Toronto needs new tools to proactively learn about emerging transportation innovations, in order to strategically regulate or incentivize them according to their potential risks and benefits.
